title: Monitor, Triage and Keep It Accurate
brief: Given a Monitor export of Meridian conversations with user feedback, produce a triage
sheet: root cause, the correct fix LAYER, owner, priority. Then fix the top five.
The layer is the whole point. The same wrong answer can be a data problem, a knowledge
store gap, a missing example query, or a question nobody could answer. Fixing it in the
wrong layer works once and rots, because the next question phrased differently breaks
again. Prose that patches a data problem is the most common version of this mistake.
review: Every row names a layer, not just a fix.
At least one item is correctly triaged as 'the data is wrong', not an agent problem.
At least one is correctly closed as expected behaviour rather than a defect.
Priorities reflect how many people hit the issue, not how annoying it was to whoever reported it.

inputs.title: Monitor export — 40 conversations with feedback
rows: Forty conversations with user feedback. Produce a triage sheet:
root cause · fix LAYER · owner · priority. Then fix the top five.
LAYERS: data · knowledge store · example query · instruction · not a defect
#  users  feedback         the question, and what came back
1    14   thumbs down      "AUM by region" — returned nothing for 'the Northeast'
2    11   thumbs down      "our AUM" — gave held-away included, no warning
3     9   thumbs down      "return last year" — answered gross, user wanted net
4     8   thumbs down      "net sales" — counted exchanges as sales
5     7   thumbs down      "AUM in California" — zero rows
6     6   thumbs down      "what we manage" — summed the daily snapshot, 682x too big
7     6   comment          "allocation by asset class" — two runs, two hierarchies
8     5   thumbs down      "last quarter" — used calendar Q, user meant fiscal
9     5   thumbs down      "month end AUM" — used 31st, market was shut
10     4   thumbs down      "flows in March" — counted PENDING and CANCELLED
11     4   comment          "top clients" — no definition of top; returned by account
12     4   thumbs down      "EUR portfolios" — added EUR to USD unconverted
13     3   thumbs down      "AUA" — answered with AUM
14     3   comment          "performance vs benchmark" — used benchmark_return as ours
15     3   thumbs down      "clients in the West" — 'out west' not recognised
16     3   comment          answer was correct but took 45 seconds
17     2   thumbs down      "cash holdings" — 'cash' not mapped to MM_CASH
18     2   thumbs down      "average account" — divided by rows not accounts
19     2   comment          "how many clients" — counted accounts
20     2   thumbs down      "fee revenue by client" — not in this data at all
21     2   comment          asked for a forecast; agent invented a trend
22     2   thumbs down      "equities" — matched EQ_US only, missed EQ_INTL and EQ_EM
23     2   comment          "YTD" — ambiguous, fiscal or calendar
24     1   thumbs down      "discretionary only" — filter silently dropped
25     1   comment          correct answer, no currency stated
26     1   thumbs down      "the Hartmann family" — no household concept exists
27     1   comment          "net new money" — phrase not recognised
28     1   thumbs down      "advisor headcount" — no such table, agent guessed
29     1   comment          answer correct; user wanted the SQL and could not see it
30     1   thumbs down      "transfers" — counted as subscriptions
31     1   comment          "since inception" — no inception date on the view
32     1   thumbs down      "Q3" — assumed FY2026 without saying so
33     1   comment          chart axis unlabelled
34     1   thumbs down      "biggest outflows" — returned inflows
35     1   comment          "per client average" — grain ambiguous, answered anyway
36     1   thumbs up        "AUM by strategy" — correct, user praised the speed
37     1   comment          "why did flows drop" — asked for a cause, got a number
38     1   thumbs down      "institutional clients" — segment name not matched
39     1   comment          timeout after 90s on a very broad question
40     1   thumbs up        "net flows FY2026 Q3" — correct and fast
Sort by how many people hit it, not by how annoyed the reporter sounded.
Not everything here is a defect. Numbers 20, 21, 26, 28 and 31 are questions
this agent should decline rather than answer — closing those correctly is worth
as much as fixing the rest.
